domain_label: Base44 Delivery & Handoff: Delivery Mechanics & the Credit Model (single-user study app on Base44)
purpose: The economics of a Base44 build pass — what an AI prompt costs, what is free, and how the delivery protocol spends credits deliberately (one-slice-one-pass, stop-after-second-fail, prefer owner keys, stop at the eight owner gates) — grounded in PROTOCOL.md's Credit discipline and carrying every Base44 pricing/behavior claim with its existing docs.base44.com [FACT-source] tag, never inventing a figure.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base scores are heuristic priors and every delivery-decision call is an ESTIMATE synthesized over PROTOCOL.md

Base44 charges message credits per AI prompt with cost scaling to how much of the app the prompt touches, per the Credits doc [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"]

every Base44 pricing/behavior fact here is reused verbatim from PROTOCOL.md's Credit-discipline [FACT-source] tags; no new pricing or platform behavior is invented, and any gap is carried as [UNKNOWN] with a route to the owner or a live docs check
the API/secret/bridge PLUMBING that realizes owner-key preference (server-side LLM routing) is extint's; this KB owns only the delivery-side spend decision
exclusions: the discuss-mode->edit-mode handoff sequence and one-strong-prompt discipline (kb2) beyond citing that planning stays outside Base44
the workspace<->GitHub sync discipline and 'unsynced = unfinished' (kb3) beyond flagging that a pass is not done until pushed
how an owner-key LLM call is wired server-side, Secret storage/rotation, backend-function/Automation implementation mechanics (owned by extint)
what a slice contains, its acceptance criteria, and which design specialists it loads (owned by the slice files, planner, and the domain specialists)
exact per-prompt credit counts (cost scales, no fixed price) and any Base44 pricing figure the docs do not state

competency_questions.question: How does Base44 charge for an AI prompt, and what does 'cost scales with how much of the app a prompt touches' mean for a build pass?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states Base44 charges message credits per AI prompt with no fixed price and cost scaling to the app-surface the prompt touches, carrying the docs.base44.com [FACT-source] tag

competency_questions.question: Which delivery actions cost zero credits, and where is a prompt's cost visible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states manual visual edits (drag, layout, text in the editor) cost zero credits and per-prompt cost is visible under More Actions -> 'Credits Used', both [FACT-source]

competency_questions.question: When do integration credits burn, and what avoids them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states integration credits burn only when the app calls Base44 BUILT-IN services (email, image gen, built-in LLM) while owner-OWN-key or backend-function calls cost zero integration credits, [FACT-source]

competency_questions.question: What does each Automation run cost, and do credits roll over?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states each Automation run = 1 integration credit and credits do not roll over, both [FACT-source]

competency_questions.question: Why is one directive one build pass, and why fix only the named thing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states one slice/directive = one build pass and the fix touches only the named thing, never a broad rebuild, because a broad rebuild touches more app-surface and costs more credits

competency_questions.question: What is the re-prompt loop and when must the agent stop looping?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the agent STOPS after the second failed fix attempt and reports honestly rather than re-prompting, because the re-prompt loop is the named credit sink

competency_questions.question: How are multiple defects from one directive handled, and how short are confirmations?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states all defects/refinements from one directive are batched into ONE pass and confirmations use the 3-line format because PROGRESS.md is the record, not chat

competency_questions.question: Why prefer the owner's own keys over built-in services, and whose decision vs whose engineering is that?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states preferring owner keys is a delivery-side spend decision (built-in LLM burns integration credits, owner-key calls don't) while the server-side routing that realizes it is extint's engineering, [FACT-source]

competency_questions.question: How is a new built-in-service dependency handled before it burns credits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states any new built-in-service (email, image gen, built-in LLM) dependency is raised as a `spend` gate question, after first asking whether an owner-key/backend-function path avoids the built-in cost

competency_questions.question: What must the agent disclose at the schedule_enable gate for a scheduled Automation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the agent states expected runs/month (= integration credits/month) at the schedule_enable gate so the owner approves a known cost

competency_questions.question: What are the eight owner gates and who decides them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: enumerates schedule_enable, credential_add, external_send, spend, host_public, data_export, security_alert, write_unlock as owner-only decisions the agent never simulates/skips/pre-approves, shipping gate-blocked work disabled/paused

competency_questions.question: What are the named credit sinks a delivery pass must avoid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names the re-prompt loop, the broad rebuild to fix a narrow thing, an unnecessary built-in-service call, and a 'describe what you built' prompt as the credit sinks, each with its free/cheaper alternative

competency_questions.question: How is a Base44 cost or behavior fact asserted honestly, and what happens when one is missing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states every Base44 credit/pricing/behavior claim carries its existing [FACT-source] tag and any gap is marked [UNKNOWN] and escalated to the owner or a live docs check (docs.base44.com -> search 'credits'), never guessed

competency_questions.question: What is the credit-discipline verdict for a build pass?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: composes one-slice-one-pass, stop-after-second-fail, free-editor/Revert-before-prompt, owner-key preference, gate-stopping with runs/month disclosure, and honesty tags into a single spend verdict for the pass

glossary.definition: Base44's per-AI-prompt charge; there is no fixed price and the cost scales with how much of the app a prompt touches, so a narrow fix costs less than a broad rebuild [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"].

The credit consumed when the app calls a Base44 BUILT-IN service (email, image generation, built-in LLM); calls made through the owner's OWN API keys or backend functions cost zero integration credits, and each Automation run = 1 integration credit [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"].

A drag, layout, or text change made directly in the Base44 editor; it costs zero credits, so cosmetic tweaks go here instead of an AI prompt [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"].

The per-prompt cost readout under More Actions -> 'Credits Used' in Base44, the ground-truth for what a given prompt actually spent [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"].

The delivery rule that a single directive/slice produces exactly one build pass which fixes only the named thing; never a broad rebuild to fix a narrow defect [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The named credit sink of repeatedly re-prompting to force a fix; the protocol STOPS after the second failed attempt and reports honestly instead of looping [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The delivery-side spend rule to route LLM calls through the owner's own configured providers rather than Base44's built-in LLM, because built-in calls burn integration credits and owner-key calls don't; the actual server-side routing is extint's engineering [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10].

One of the eight owner gates; the point at which any new cost-incurring decision (a new built-in-service dependency, a scheduled Automation's runs/month) is surfaced to the owner for approval, never pre-approved by the agent [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10].

schedule_enable, credential_add, external_send, spend, host_public, data_export, security_alert, write_unlock — decisions only the owner makes; the agent never simulates, skips, or pre-approves one, and gate-blocked work ships disabled/paused [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10].

Base44's rule that unused credits expire rather than accumulating across the billing period, so a scheduled Automation's monthly integration-credit draw is a standing, non-bankable cost [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"].

nodes.definition: Frame every delivery question as: a directive becomes exactly one build pass, and each pass deliberately spends credits. Base44 charges message credits per AI prompt with no fixed price and cost scaling to how much of the app the prompt touches [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"], so the delivery protocol treats prompts as the scarce paid resource and pushes everything it can to the free surfaces (planning outside Base44, the visual editor, version-history Revert, code audits via GitHub/Codex). Getting this frame wrong — treating a prompt as free or rebuilding broadly to fix narrowly — is the most expensive delivery error, so it is fixed first [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10].

included: the build pass as the unit of spend
credits as the scarce resource the protocol conserves
excluded: the concrete per-fact credit rules (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in Base44's credit model or a new free surface revises the frame

pros.claim: Fixing the paid-vs-free frame first stops a pass from spending a prompt where a free edit or Revert would do
pros.example: deciding early that a color tweak is a free visual edit, not an AI prompt

cons.claim: The frame is a doctrine abstraction, not a measured cost, so an unusual prompt can blur which surface is cheapest
cons.example: a change that is 'cosmetic' but also alters logic, which is not a pure free edit

failure_modes: treating an AI prompt as a free action
rebuilding broadly to fix a narrow defect
acceptance_tests: the frame names the paid-prompt-vs-free-surface split, the build pass as the spend unit, and the scale-with-app-surface cost rule with the docs.base44.com [FACT-source] tag
revisit_triggers: Base44 changes its credit model
a new free editing surface appears
a prompt's cost is surprisingly high in Credits Used

nodes.definition: State the charging model: Base44 charges message credits per AI prompt; there is no fixed price and the cost scales with how much of the app a prompt touches [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"]. This is why a scoped, single-slice prompt is cheaper than a sweeping one, and why the delivery protocol keeps each pass narrow. The exact per-prompt credit count is not a fixed figure and is not invented here; when a specific number is needed it is read from the live 'Credits Used' readout, not guessed [UNKNOWN-until-read].

excluded: the exact per-prompt count (read from Credits Used)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a Base44 pricing change or a measured Credits Used figure revises the model

pros.claim: Knowing cost scales with app-surface makes narrow prompts a direct cost lever
pros.example: scoping a prompt to one component instead of the whole page to spend fewer credits

cons.claim: Without a fixed price, cost is only knowable after the fact via Credits Used, so pre-estimates are ESTIMATE
cons.example: assuming a prompt will be cheap and finding a high charge in Credits Used

failure_modes: assuming a fixed per-prompt price
asserting an invented credit count
acceptance_tests: the model states message-credit-per-prompt, no fixed price, and cost scaling with app-surface, carrying the [FACT-source] tag and marking any specific count [UNKNOWN-until-read]

nodes.definition: Record the free surface: manual visual edits — drag, layout, text changes made directly in the editor — cost zero credits [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"]. Cosmetic work (text, colors, spacing) therefore goes through the visual editor, never an AI prompt. This is a primary spend lever: an AI prompt spent on a cosmetic tweak is a wasted credit when the free editor would have done it.

included: cosmetic tweaks route to the visual editor

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change to what the visual editor can do for free revises the boundary

pros.claim: Routing cosmetic tweaks to the free editor removes a whole class of wasted prompts
pros.example: recoloring a header by hand instead of prompting the AI to recolor it

cons.claim: The free-edit boundary is only cosmetic; a tweak that also changes behavior is not free and needs a pass

failure_modes: spending an AI prompt on a cosmetic change
treating a behavioral change as a free visual edit
acceptance_tests: the node states manual visual edits cost zero credits and cosmetic tweaks route to the editor not a prompt, [FACT-source]
revisit_triggers: Base44 changes the visual editor's free scope
a cosmetic change turns out to touch logic

This makes 'built-in vs owner-key' a direct cost decision at the delivery layer. The delivery protocol prefers the owner-key/backend-function path wherever the slice permits; the server-side wiring that realizes it is extint's, not this KB's.

nodes.definition: State the Automation cost: each Automation run = 1 integration credit [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"]. A scheduled Automation therefore has a knowable monthly cost equal to its runs/month, which must be disclosed to the owner at the schedule_enable gate before it is turned on. nodes.definition: Record the rollover rule: credits do not roll over [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"]. Unused credits expire rather than banking, so a standing cost like a scheduled Automation's monthly integration-credit draw is a recurring, non-recoverable spend, and there is no case for 'saving up' credits by deferring work. This sharpens the owner-key preference and the runs/month disclosure: the monthly draw is real every month.

nodes.definition: Enforce the core delivery rule: one slice/directive = one build pass, and the pass fixes only the named thing — never a broad rebuild to fix a narrow defect [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10]. Because prompt cost scales with app-surface touched [FACT-source: docs.base44.com Credits doc, retrieved 2026-07-10; docs site restructured, old paths 404 — enter via docs.base44.com and search "credits"], a broad rebuild is strictly more expensive than a scoped fix, so 'fix the named thing only' is a spend rule, not just tidiness. This node is the highest-leverage credit control in the pass.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a directive that legitimately needs multi-surface work revises the scope test

pros.claim: A scoped one-thing fix touches the least app-surface and therefore costs the fewest credits
pros.example: fixing one broken button by naming it, not re-prompting the whole page

cons.claim: Some directives genuinely span surfaces, and forcing them into one narrow pass can under-fix
cons.example: a defect whose real cause is upstream, where a truly narrow fix misses it

failure_modes: rebuilding broadly to fix a narrow defect
splitting one directive into many prompts and multiplying cost
acceptance_tests: the node states one directive = one pass fixing only the named thing, refusing the broad rebuild, cited to PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline
revisit_triggers: a directive spans multiple surfaces
a narrow fix repeatedly misses the real cause
Credits Used shows a pass touched too much

nodes.definition: Enforce the loop stop: if a fix needs multiple attempts, STOP after the second failed attempt and report honestly instead of looping — the re-prompt loop is the named credit sink [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10]. Each re-prompt is another paid message credit, so a loop silently drains credits without converging. In continuous mode the branch halts and says plainly what is broken and blocked-on-whom while other clear items proceed [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Continuous mode, added 2026-07-10].

included: stop after the second failed fix attempt

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change to the failed-attempt threshold revises the stop rule

cons.claim: A hard two-attempt cap can stop just before a fix that a third attempt would have landed
cons.example: a nearly-correct fix abandoned at attempt two

failure_modes: re-prompting a failing fix past the second attempt
hiding the failure instead of reporting it honestly
acceptance_tests: the node states the agent stops after the second failed fix attempt and reports honestly, naming the re-prompt loop as the credit sink, cited to PROTOCOL.md
revisit_triggers: fixes routinely need a third attempt
the credit sink is observed in Credits Used

nodes.definition: Enforce batching: all defects and refinements given in one directive are addressed in ONE build pass — the directive is already written for that [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline, added 2026-07-10]. Splitting a directive's items into separate prompts multiplies the paid message credits for work that a single pass covers. Batching composes with one-slice-one-pass: one directive, one pass, all its named items.

included: all named defects/refinements from one directive in one pass
excluded: work belonging to a later slice (leave it, note in PROGRESS.md)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a directive too large for one pass revises the batching bound

pros.claim: Batching a directive's items into one pass avoids paying per-item prompt costs

cons.claim: A very large directive can overflow one pass, and cramming it risks touching too much app-surface
cons.example: a directive with ten unrelated items where one pass sprawls

failure_modes: issuing a separate prompt per defect
pulling later-slice work into the pass while batching
acceptance_tests: the node states all defects/refinements from one directive are batched into one pass, cited to PROTOCOL.md Credit discipline
revisit_triggers: a directive is too large for one pass

conflict_axes.name: paid_prompt_vs_free_surface
conflict_axes.description: An AI prompt is a paid message credit while the visual editor, Revert, and code audits are free, so any work that could go to a free surface should.
poles: prompt the AI for the change
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: send cosmetic tweaks to the free editor and audits to GitHub/Codex; spend a prompt only where no free surface suffices

conflict_axes.name: cosmetic_prompt_vs_free_editor
conflict_axes.description: A cosmetic text/color/spacing change can be prompted or done by hand in the editor for zero credits.
poles: make it in the free editor
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: do all cosmetic edits in the free visual editor and never spend an AI prompt on them

conflict_axes.name: builtin_convenience_vs_integration_credit_cost
conflict_axes.description: Base44's built-in services are the convenient default but burn integration credits the owner-key path avoids.
poles: route through the owner's own key
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer the owner-key/backend-function path where the slice permits and flag an unavoidable built-in as a spend gate

conflict_axes.name: narrow_fix_vs_broad_rebuild
conflict_axes.description: A narrow fix touches the least app-surface and costs the fewest credits; a broad rebuild is more thorough but strictly more expensive.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fix only the named thing; a broad rebuild to fix a narrow defect is the expensive error

conflict_axes.name: keep_trying_vs_stop_the_credit_sink
conflict_axes.description: Chasing a stubborn fix tempts another prompt while each re-prompt is another paid credit with no guaranteed convergence.
poles: stop after the second failed attempt
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stop after the second failed fix and report honestly; the re-prompt loop is the named credit sink

conflict_axes.name: silent_schedule_vs_disclosed_recurring_cost
conflict_axes.description: A scheduled Automation could be enabled silently or its monthly integration-credit draw disclosed for owner approval.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state expected runs/month (= integration credits/month) at the schedule_enable gate before the owner flips it

conflict_axes.name: pre_approve_vs_stop_at_gate
conflict_axes.description: Momentum pulls toward pre-approving an owner gate to keep building, but gates are owner-only decisions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never simulate, skip, or pre-approve a gate; ship gate-blocked work disabled/paused until the owner flips it

conflict_axes.name: assert_now_vs_tag_or_mark_unknown
conflict_axes.description: A missing Base44 cost fact tempts a plausible guess versus carrying it as [UNKNOWN] with a live-docs route.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never guess a Base44 price or behavior; carry the [FACT-source] tag or mark [UNKNOWN] and route to the owner or docs.base44.com

conflict_axes.name: handoff_spend_decision_vs_extint_routing
conflict_axes.description: Whether to spend a built-in credit is a handoff delivery decision; how the owner-key call is wired is extint engineering, and the two must not be conflated.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: handoff owns whether to prompt/spend and prefer owner keys; extint owns the server-side routing that realizes it
